Layer wise importance sampled mini batches (LADIES)

Source: R/subgraph-loaders.R
ladies_loader.Rd

Builds node mini batches by layer dependent importance sampling (Zou et al. 2019), the successor of FastGCN (Chen, Ma and Xiao 2018). For each batch, batch_size training nodes are the seeds (layer 0). Going from layer \(l\) to layer \(l + 1\), candidates are the sources of edges into the layer \(l\) nodes, and layer_sizes[l + 1] of them are drawn without replacement with probability $$p(u) \propto \sum_{v \in S_l} \hat A_{vu}^2,$$ where \(\hat A = D^{-1/2}(A + I)D^{-1/2}\) (degrees are weighted in degrees plus one). Layer \(l + 1\) is the sampled set plus the layer \(l\) nodes. Each kept edge \(u \to v\) gets the weight \(\hat A_{vu} / p(u)\), normalized to sum to one over the incoming edges of \(v\) in that layer (the row normalization of LADIES).

Usage

ladies_loader(
  g,
  batch_size = 64L,
  layer_sizes = c(256L, 256L),
  shuffle = TRUE,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

g

A graph_data object with train_mask (training passes its own masks to the loader).

batch_size

Seed nodes per batch.

layer_sizes

Nodes sampled per layer, one entry per model layer.

shuffle

Shuffle the seeds each epoch.

seed

Optional integer seed; batches of epoch \(e\) use seed + e.

Value

A ladies_loader, to pass as loader to train_graph_model() or to loader_batches().

Details

The batch is one graph_data subgraph that holds the edges of all layers together (with the weight of the first layer that kept an edge), so it works with any model in train_graph_model(); this is a common simplification of the layer by layer bipartite blocks of the paper. Models should read edge_weight (for example gnn_model("sage") or gnn_model("graph"); gcn_conv normalizes the weights again). Only the seeds carry train_mask, so the loss uses the seeds only.

References

Zou et al. (2019) Layer-dependent importance sampling for training deep and large graph convolutional networks. NeurIPS. Chen, Ma and Xiao (2018) FastGCN: fast learning with graph convolutional networks via importance sampling. ICLR.

Examples

g <- split_nodes(dataset_karate(), seed = 1)
ld <- ladies_loader(g, batch_size = 8, layer_sizes = c(10, 10), seed = 1)
b <- loader_batches(ld, epoch = 1)[[1]]
c(nodes = b$num_nodes, seeds = sum(b$train_mask))
#> nodes seeds 
#>    17     8
